Spectral fits and held-out transmittance

The inversions use reflectance only. Every leaf in the validation set also has a measured transmittance, which provides a direct out-of-sample check. Each posterior draw is pushed through PROSPECT-D to predict T, and the prediction is compared with the measurement. A model that has the right structure and the right uncertainty should predict T about as well as it fits R, with 90% predictive intervals covering about 90% of the measured values.

Spectral fits

All five backends give practically identical posterior predictive spectra (see Backends), so only Stan is shown here. The full table below covers every backend.

Transmittance as validation

Reading the transmittance check. Averaged over leaves, the reflectance fit has RMSE nan with nan% in-sample predictive coverage. The held-out transmittance prediction has RMSE nan and only nan% coverage. The T errors are smooth and systematic rather than noisy: they are model-structure and parameter errors, not measurement noise. That is exactly what the iid model’s single σ cannot describe. It also matches the known weakness of reflectance-only PROSPECT inversion: N, Cw and Cm trade off against each other, and R alone cannot pin down how light is split between transmittance and absorptance. Practical consequences:

  1. Fitting R and T jointly is much better when T exists. The forward model already returns both in every backend, so this only changes the likelihood.
  2. When only R is available, the posterior must be widened honestly. That is the job of the structured error models on the Error models page, which this check can then evaluate.
